text.scopeInPlaceholder: e.g. From the pick face to handover to the driver

sipoc: Who provides what the process needs
5 to 7 steps, each starting with a verb

raci.A: Accountable: owns the result, one per activity

kano.functional: If the feature is there, how does the customer feel?
kano.dysfunctional: If the feature is not there, how does the customer feel?

M: Expected. Missing it makes customers angry; having it earns no thanks.
O: The more, the better: satisfaction rises with every step.
A: Not expected. Having it delights; missing it costs nothing.
I: Customers do not care either way. Do not spend on it.
R: Customers would rather not have it.
Q: The two answers contradict each other: ask again.

copq: Rework, scrap, re-packing, before the customer sees it

define: The problem has a number, a time frame and the gap to the target.
The goal is measurable and has a date.
Scope in and out is written down and agreed.
The SIPOC shows 5 to 7 process steps, from supplier to customer.
Each CTQ comes from the voice of the customer and has a specification.
Roles are agreed in the RACI: one person accountable for each activity.
measure: Every CTQ has an operational definition, with photos where it helps.
A data collection plan says what is recorded, where, by whom and how often.
The measurement was checked: two people judged the same cases and agreed.
The baseline covers at least two to four weeks.
DPMO, sigma level, RTY and the cost of poor quality are calculated.
The goal is confirmed or adjusted with the sponsor.
analyze: The team walked the process where the work is done.
A Pareto shows which causes carry most of the defects.
Possible causes were listed and narrowed down with data.
The root causes are proven with data, not with opinion.
The 5 Whys end at a cause the team can act on.
The sponsor agrees which root causes the Improve phase will attack.
improve: Each countermeasure attacks a proven root cause.
Solutions were chosen by effort and impact.
A pilot ran with the same definition and the same log as the baseline.
The pilot result is compared with the baseline, and the change is clear.
Side effects on time, cost and safety are checked and accepted.
The roll-out plan has owners and dates.
control: The new method is in the standard work and in the training.
The control plan says what is measured, how often, by whom and what happens when it goes out of control.
A control chart with limits from the improved process is running.
The savings are confirmed with finance.
The process owner has taken over the result.
Lessons learned are shared and the project is closed.

tips: A charter with a number, a time frame and a gap. If the problem has no number, the project has no end.
Close each tollgate with the sponsor.
Tick what is done; a phase closes only when the list is complete, or with a written reason the sponsor signs.
Watch the days in a phase.
More than 45 days in one phase usually means the project is stuck: ask what blocks the next tollgate.
Hard savings are euros that leave the cost lines; soft savings are written down with an estimate, not added to the total.
Every line of the control plan goes to the Action Tracker with its owner, so the result stays after the project closes.

charter.problem: In weeks 36 to 38, 0.57% of outbound units left the hub damaged (104 of 18,400 in week 38) against 0.30% promised to the customer. Credits cost about €1,150 a week.
charter.goal: 0.30% or lower by week 46, without longer loading times.
charter.scopeIn: From the pick face to handover to the driver.
charter.team: Shift leads early and late, two loaders, one driver, quality coordinator.

o: Damage log by stage and cause

ctq.ctq: Routes with load bars and photo

rows.activity: Train the loaders at each dock
Log damage by stage and cause
Run the daily p-chart and react

kano.feature: Photo of the parcel at the door

savings.soft: Fewer customer complaints, less re-packing on the late shift.

control.method: Damage log, p-chart with limits from the pilot weeks
control.reaction: A day above the upper limit: check the same shift and run 5 Whys within 24 hours.

control.what: Load bars set after the last wall
control.reaction: No photo: the vehicle does not leave until the shift lead has set the bar and noted why.

control.spec: Heavy low, fragile high, no gaps
control.method: Floor check against the dock picture
control.reaction: Two failed checks in a row: retrain the team at that dock the same week.

improve.reason: Side effects were checked on the late shift only; the early shift is checked in the first two weeks of Control.

projects.title: Late routes on the morning wave

charter.problem: In weeks 30 to 37, 9.4% of morning routes left the depot after 07:45 (113 of 1,200) against 3% agreed with the customer. Each late route costs about €40 in overtime and redelivery.
charter.goal: 3% or fewer late departures by week 50.
charter.scopeIn: From the trailer arriving at the depot to the van leaving the gate.
charter.team: Depot lead, two drivers, sorter team lead, dispatcher.

ctq.need: Parcels arrive in the promised window

savings.soft: Drivers start calmer, fewer calls to customer service.

measure.reason: The measurement check is repeated with the new scanner log in week 1 of Analyze.

projects.title: Fewer no-shows at the airport hotel

charter.problem: From July to September, 6.8% of guaranteed reservations were no-shows (612 of 9,000 room nights) against 4% in the budget. A room that could have been resold costs about €95.
charter.goal: 4% or lower from March, without more cancellations at the desk.
charter.scopeIn: From the booking to the night audit of the arrival day.
charter.team: Front office manager, two receptionists, night auditor, reservations agent.

p: Charge the no-show at night audit

savings.soft: Better forecast for housekeeping and breakfast.

projects.title: Picking errors in the small-parts zone

charter.problem: In weeks 38 to 41, 0.42% of order lines in the small-parts zone were picked wrong (210 of 50,000) against 0.15% in the service agreement.
charter.scopeIn: Small-parts zone, from the pick list to the packing table.
charter.team: Shift lead, three pickers, IT key user.
